content.title: Illinois’ Season Ends at the Final Four with 71-62 Loss to #7 Connecticut
content.text: INDIANAPOLIS, Ind. – The Illinois men's basketball team's run through March Madness ended Saturday at the Final Four. The Illini fell to Connecticut, 71-62, in the national semifinal. Illinois (28-9) battled to get within four points with 1:38 to play in front of the Illini-heavy crowd, but could not finish the comeback. Keaton Wagler led Illinois with 20 points and eight rebounds, while Tomislav Ivisic added 16 points and six boards. A 10-0 second-half run over 4+ minutes put the Illini back in the game. Andrej Stojakovic capped the run with 5:02 left with a lay-in that followed eight straight Illinois free throws to make the score 57-53 in UConn's favor. Wagler then got Illinois back within four points on a layup with 1:38 left and again brought the game within four on a three-pointer with 38 seconds left. Connecticut countered with points on both of its possessions' following Wagler's makes and advanced to Monday's national championship game. Illinois took its first and only lead with 7:54 remaining in the first half at 22-21 on an Ivisic three-pointer. UConn finished the half on a 16-7 run to take an eight-point lead into the break. Connecticut (34-5) had three players in double figures, led by Tarris Reed Jr.'s 17 points and 11 rebounds. Braylon Mullins scored 15 and Solo Ball had 13 points. Illinois advanced to the Final Four for the sixth time in program history. The team's 28 wins were the fourth-most in program history. HIGHLIGHTS PRESS CONFERENCE POSTGAME NOTES Player Keaton Wagler led the Illini in scoring with 20 points, grabbed a team-high eight rebounds and dished out two assists. First freshman guard to post 20+ points and 8+ rebounds in an NCAA Tournament National Semifinal since Memphis' Derrick Rose (25 points and 8 rebounds) vs. UCLA on April 5, 2008. Fifth freshman with 20+ points and 8+ rebounds in a Final Four game since 1995, joining Paolo Banchero (Duke, 2022), Derrick Rose (Memphis, 2008), Greg Oden (Ohio State, 2007), and Carmelo Anthony (2x, Syracuse, 2003). 11th game of the season with 20+ points, breaking the Illinois freshman record set last season by Kasparas Jakucionis. 29th consecutive game with 10+ points, and his team-leading 34th double-figure scoring game, overall. Averaged 19.1 points since Dec. 6. 23rd game with multiple 3-pointers, fifth consecutive. Moved to third on Illinois' all-time season scoring list with 663 points 1. 736 - Terrence Shannon Jr. (2024) 2. 668 - Don Freeman (1966) 3. 663 - Keaton Wagler (2026) 4. 660 - Andy Kaufmann (1991) 5. 647 - Nick Anderson (1989) Tied Illinois freshman single-season record for total 3-pointers made with 87 joining Jalen Coleman-Lands who set it 2015-16, and moved into the all-time single-season top 5 at Illinois. Tomislav Ivisic tallied 16 points, secured seven rebounds, blocked one shot and had a steal. 19th game of the season with 10+ points and 41st of his career. Sixth double-digit scoring effort in seven career NCAA Tournament games. Averaged 14.7 points in his career in the NCAA Tournament. 15th game of the season with multiple 3-pointers. 105 3-pointers are the most in the nation among 7-footers over the last two seasons. David Mirkovic scored six points, secured five rebounds and blocked a career- and team-high three shots. Averaged 13 points and 9.8 rebounds in the NCAA Tournament. Extended his Illinois freshman record for total rebounds to 297 boards. Broke the mark of 272 set by Kofi Cockburn in 2019-20 vs. Houston in Sweet 16. Finished No. 3 on the Illini freshman scoring list with 493 points. Recorded a career-high 3 blocks, the first game of his career with multiple rejections. Andrej Stojakovic added nine points, brought in a team-high eight rebounds and had an assist. Averaged 13.8 points in the NCAA tournament.
